$description: Layout references for a site's pages, keyed to what the visitor came to do. Structure only: which part leads, the order of the parts, where the action sits and how the page ends. Every look value of a page comes from the brand's tokens and its G4 rules, never from this file. A layout is a reference to start from, not a template to fill in.
how_to_use: Start from the visitor's job, as brief/BRIEF.md and FACTS.md state it, and never from how a liked site looked. Pick the item whose `job` is the one this visitor came to do.
Take structure only: which part leads, the order of the parts, where the action sits and how the page ends. Every look value comes from the tokens and the G4 rules; nothing in this file sets one.

Record the choice on the page as `<body data-layout="<id>">`. When no item fits the job, write `own:<word>` and give the reason on the page's card; the lint warns, so the references stay a starting point and never a menu.
A layout is a reference, not a template. Move, drop or merge parts when the material says so, and drop a part that has nothing real to hold instead of filling it.
Equal tiles in threes, a label over every heading and the stock hero, steps, questions and call-to-action band are tells, not layouts. page-tells.json names them and the page check warns about them.

items.job: Join, subscribe or sign up when there is nothing to compare.
items.leads_with: The one thing the visitor gets, stated in one sentence, with the form or button that gets it right beside it.
parts: The offer in one plain sentence
The form or the button itself, in the first view
What happens right after they submit
The one fact that removes the last doubt, such as who sends it and how to leave
items.action: The action is the page: it sits in the first view and comes back once at the end only if the page scrolls.
items.ends_with: A short line on what the visitor will receive and how to leave, with the sender's contact details.
items.not_for: Anything the visitor has to compare, price or understand before committing.

items.job: Understand how a service will run for them before handing it something important.
items.leads_with: The outcome for the visitor in their own words, with the first stage already in view beneath it.
parts: The outcome the visitor is after
The stages in the order the visitor lives them, each with the real artefact they will hold or see
The stage that carries the risk given the most room, and the routine ones given little
What the visitor does and what the provider does at each stage
The cost and the time, placed beside the stage they belong to
The questions the stages leave open
items.action: The action appears after the stage where the visitor has understood enough to start, and again at the end.
items.ends_with: The last stage as the visitor will meet it, then how to begin and who they will deal with.
items.not_for: Something bought in one click, or a tool the visitor can try at once.

items.job: Choose from a range and buy.
items.leads_with: The range itself, with a way to narrow it down, rather than a statement about the shop.
parts: The range, each item carrying what a buyer needs to compare
Ways to narrow or sort the range
One item opened out with its facts, its options and its price
Delivery, returns and payment, placed where the buyer decides
Help choosing for the buyer who does not know where to start
items.action: Buying sits on the item rather than on the list; the list exists to lead the buyer to an item.
items.ends_with: Delivery, returns and how to reach a person, then the way back to the range.
items.not_for: A single product, or a service the visitor cannot see on a shelf.

items.leads_with: The product itself, shown in use, with its name and its price in the first view.
parts: The product shown as the buyer will use it
What it does for them, in the order they ask
The facts checked before paying, such as what is in the box, what it fits and what it costs
Proof from people who already have it
Delivery, returns and warranty
The questions that stop a purchase
items.action: The buying action is in the first view and comes back wherever the page has just given the buyer a reason.
items.ends_with: Delivery and returns, then the buying action once more.
items.not_for: A range to choose from, or a service that needs explaining before it can be bought.

items.job: Be persuaded by an argument or learn a subject.
items.leads_with: The claim, or the question the whole page answers, in the author's own sentence.
parts: The claim or the question
The argument in sections, each opening on its conclusion
The evidence beside the claim it supports, such as a figure, a quotation or a case
The point where the argument is weakest, said plainly
What follows if the reader agrees
items.action: One action comes after the argument, offered as the next thing to read or do, and nothing interrupts the reading before it.
items.ends_with: What to do next with what they have read, and who wrote it.
items.not_for: A visitor who came to do something rather than to read.

items.job: Trust a person or a small practice before getting in touch.
items.leads_with: The person, by name, saying in their own words what they do and who for.
parts: Who they are and who they work with
What they do, in the plain words a client would use
How they work, as a client meets it
One or two real examples, with names or places where those may be used
The facts a cautious visitor checks, such as qualifications, registration and how prices are set
How to reach them and how soon they reply
items.action: A way to get in touch that suits the visitor, a name with a number or an address, sits near the top and again at the end.
items.ends_with: The contact details once more, with when the person answers.
items.not_for: A business with many staff, a range to buy from or a product to try.

items.leads_with: The tool's real screen doing real work, not a picture of the idea.
parts: The real screen in use, showing what it just produced
One task done from start to finish
The few things it does that others do not, each on a real screen
What it connects to and where the data lives
What it costs and what the free try includes
Documentation, support and what to do when it breaks
items.action: Starting is the action: signing up or opening the tool sits in the first view and comes back after the task has been shown.
items.ends_with: How to start, what the first hour looks like and where to ask for help.
items.not_for: Software the visitor will never touch themselves, or one that cannot be shown working.

items.leads_with: A way to search or filter the whole set, already working, with the first results beneath it.
parts: Search and filters that answer the question the visitor brought
The results, each carrying the facts that tell the items apart
A clear state for no results, with a next move
One item opened out, with a way back to the same results
How the set is kept, what it includes and how current it is
items.action: Finding is the action: each result leads to its item, and contact or submission sits beside the item.
items.ends_with: What the set covers and how often it changes, with how to add to it or correct it.
items.not_for: A short range browsed in one look, or a visitor who does not yet know what they are looking for.

items.leads_with: The next dates or free slots, with the place or the format, ready to take.
parts: The next dates or free times, soonest first
What each one is and who it is for
The place or the link, and how to get there or join
What it costs and what the visitor needs to bring or know
How to cancel or move a booking
Who runs it
items.action: Booking sits on each date or slot and works without leaving the list.
items.ends_with: The cancellation terms and who to ask, with the next dates again for a visitor none of them suited.
items.not_for: Something with no fixed time, or a visitor who first has to be persuaded it is worth their time.

items.leads_with: Whether the place is open today, with its hours and its address, answered at once.
parts: Today's hours and the address
The route by each way people arrive, with a map that opens in the visitor's own app
What it is like inside, shown with real photographs of the place
What to know before coming, such as bookings, access, cost and what to bring
Contact for the questions the page does not answer
items.action: Getting there is the action: directions open in the visitor's own map, and a phone number or a booking sits beside them.
items.ends_with: The address, the hours and the access once more, with a contact for a change of plan.
items.not_for: A business the visitor deals with from home, or one with no fixed place.

items.job: Hire someone on the strength of their work.
items.leads_with: The best work itself, with the client and the result named.
parts: A few chosen pieces, each with the client, the problem and the result
One piece opened out: what was asked, what was done, what changed
Who did the work and how they work with a client
What they take on and what they turn down
Who will say so, as named clients or a reference the visitor can call
items.action: Getting in touch sits beside the work and again at the end, and says what to send first.
items.ends_with: How to start a project with them, what to send and how soon they reply.
items.not_for: Work that cannot be shown or described, or a visitor who wants a price list.

items.job: Decide when doubts about cost, risk or rules stand in the way.
items.leads_with: The doubt that stops most people, asked in their words and answered in the first lines.
parts: The questions in the order people drop out, each answered in full
The numbers behind each answer, such as what it costs, what is refunded and what is guaranteed
The rule or the clause each answer rests on, named and linked
Who to ask when the question is not here
The action, once the doubts are answered
items.action: The action waits until the doubts are answered and then sits directly after the answer that settles the last one.
items.ends_with: Who to ask when a question is missing, and the action once more.
items.not_for: A visitor with no doubts yet, or a page that lists questions nobody asked.
